label: Multi-pool hooks
summary: Use one hook across several PoolKeys with explicit registration, isolation and cross-pool accounting rules.
requiredFacts: Allowed PoolKeys, registration and retirement lifecycle and whether new pools are permissionless
Every storage, liability, nonce, claim and configuration key that must include pool identity
Which behavior is isolated per pool and which behavior intentionally reads or moves value across pools
Cross-pool call ordering, nested unlock behavior, reentrancy boundaries and failure atomicity
Per-pool metadata, fee, authority, emergency exit and indexer reconstruction
requiredTests: Two or more pools with colliding currencies, fees, ticks and adversarial configuration
Pool-scoped liability, claim, nonce, authority and accounting isolation
Nested, reordered and reverted cross-pool operations with atomic failure behavior
Registration, duplicate registration, retirement and emergency exit per pool
Indexer reconstruction and metadata identity for every PoolKey
risks: Missing PoolKey domain separation can leak authority or liabilities across pools
Nested cross-pool actions expand reentrancy and partial-failure complexity
Shared upgrades or emergency controls can affect unrelated pools simultaneously
